text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The authorities have freed outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) president Abassi Madani. The gesture mirrors a strong state of law in Algeria combining the rigour of the law with a spirit of justice and tolerance.
- Madani's release was a clemency measure undertaken by the authorities in the framework of an appeasment dynamic agreed on by most political parties.
- The local elections will be held on October 23.
- Madani was set free after six years in jail. The release reflected the evolution of Algeria's political situation, mainly since plural presidential elections in 1995.
- Gunmen shot dead a local politician on Monday near his home in Boumerdes region, 40 km (25 miles) east of Algiers. A bomb exploded the same day in Algiers wounding several people.

- Madani's release was a "political freeing". The release, even contingent to conditions, could not happen if there were no contacts with the authorities. Politically, no one could believe that this decision was taken without a prior accord.
